live.name: NICKEL FOXCROFT
live.headline: NICKEL FOXCROFT: a threat actor known by many names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists NICKEL FOXCROFT under many aliases, including APT37 and ScarCruft, and names eight tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: NICKEL FOXCROFT is the Secureworks name for a threat actor tracked under many other names.
Its aliases include APT37, ATK4, Group 123, InkySquid, Moldy Pisces, Operation Daybreak, Operaton Erebus, RICOCHET CHOLLIMA, Reaper, ScarCruft, TA-RedAnt and Venus 121.
The catalogue links eight tools to the actor: Bluelight, Chinotto, GOLDBACKDOOR, KevDroid, KoSpy, PoorWeb, ROKRAT and final1stpy.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: NICKEL FOXCROFT
next.headline: NICKEL FOXCROFT (APT37, ScarCruft): a long-running espionage group focused on Korea
next.in_short: Vendors describe NICKEL FOXCROFT, better known as APT37 or ScarCruft, as a North Korea-linked espionage group active since 2012. It mostly targets South Korea and uses phishing, shortcut files and cloud-based control.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists NICKEL FOXCROFT under many other names, including APT37, ScarCruft, Reaper, InkySquid, Group 123 and RICOCHET CHOLLIMA.
ESET says ScarCruft, also known as APT37 or Reaper, has operated since at least 2012 and is suspected to be a North Korean espionage group.
CrowdStrike calls its RICOCHET CHOLLIMA profile a DPRK-nexus targeted intrusion adversary involved in espionage since at least 2016.
Lookout attributes the KoSpy Android spyware to APT37 with medium confidence. It notes that North Korean groups share infrastructure, targeting and techniques, which makes attribution harder.

Genians notes that some researchers class KONNI, Kimsuky and APT37 as one group. Genians says they overlap in targets and infrastructure. The MSMT report, as cited by Genians, assesses Kimsuky and KONNI as distinct groups.
CrowdStrike says its observed operations have almost exclusively targeted the Republic of Korea. It assesses they focus on government officials, NGOs, academics and journalists.
AhnLab's ASEC says the group targets individuals such as human rights activists, reporters and North Korean defectors.

360 Advanced Threat Research Institute says a 2024 campaign hit government personnel and corporations in South Korea and Asia, with strategic industries such as aerospace, chemicals and healthcare also named.
ESET reports a supply-chain attack on a video game platform aimed at the Yanbian region of China. It infers that the main targets are ethnic Koreans there, most likely refugees or defectors.
Genians reports a March 2025 spear phishing campaign against activists focused on North Korea, with lures posing as a South Korean national security think tank.
Phishing emails with ZIP files hiding malicious shortcut (LNK) files are a common start. They launch a chain of scripts that loads the RokRat remote access tool in memory.
RokRat uses legitimate cloud services such as pCloud, Yandex and Dropbox for command and control. It captures screenshots and can collect files.
AhnLab's ASEC describes a Hangul document exploiting the old flaw CVE-2017-8291. It hid a payload in a JPEG image and installed a backdoor called M2RAT, which logs keystrokes and takes screenshots.
Zscaler says one campaign, Ruby Jumper, spreads through removable media to reach air-gapped networks. Zscaler also says this was, to its knowledge, the first time APT37 abused Zoho WorkDrive.

Zscaler also describes chains that start from a shortcut or a Windows help file. They drop the Rustonotto and Chinotto backdoors and then FadeStealer, which collects files, keystrokes, screenshots and audio.
Lookout describes KoSpy, Android spyware disguised as utility apps and spread through Google Play and Firebase Firestore.
S2W judged from analysis of techniques that a December 2020 watering-hole attack, which delivered a ROKRAT variant, related to ScarCruft. This is a judgement, not a confirmed attribution.
AhnLab's ASEC saw the M2RAT phishing attacks begin in January 2023.
ESET says the game platform attack was probably ongoing since late 2024. It says an Android version of the BirdCall backdoor was delivered through trojanized games.
Genians says the first observed Operation ToyBox Story spear phishing attack was on March 8, 2025. It delivered the RoKRAT malware.
Zscaler published its Ruby Jumper report on 2026-02-26.
Treat unexpected shortcut files inside archives, and unsolicited documents sent to activists, journalists and researchers, as suspect.
Monitor for scripting activity and for unusual traffic to cloud storage services from endpoints.
